classification.difficultyReason: Standardise two weights, subtract cumulative table probabilities and multiply by the population size.

content.prompt: The weights of 10 000 newborn babies in NSW are normally distributed. These weights have a mean of 3.1 kg and a standard deviation of 0.35 kg.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the probability that a randomly chosen baby has a weight between 3.24 kg and 3.66 kg? Use the standard normal table and give your answer correct to 4 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be a baby's weight in kilograms.
$$\begin{aligned}z_{\text{lower}}&=\frac{3.24-3.1}{0.35}\\z_{\text{lower}}&=0.4\\z_{\text{upper}}&=\frac{3.66-3.1}{0.35}\\z_{\text{upper}}&=1.6\end{aligned}$$
Using the standard normal table,
$$\begin{aligned}P(3.24<X<3.66)&=P(0.4<Z<1.6)\\P(3.24<X<3.66)&=P(Z\le1.6)-P(Z\le0.4)\\P(3.24<X<3.66)&\approx0.9452-0.6554\\P(3.24<X<3.66)&\approx0.2898.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many of the 10 000 newborn babies would have a weight between 3.24 kg and 3.66 kg?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Expected number}&=10\,000\times0.2898\\\text{Expected number}&=2898.\end{aligned}$$
Approximately 2898 babies would have a weight between 3.24 kg and 3.66 kg.
